newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German industry orders data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German industry orders data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to German industry orders data for February. The data showed a 0.2 pct month-on-month rise versus a 2.7 percent gain in January.
ARMIN KAYSER, Economist at Swiss Bank in Frankfurt

"It is quite small. The markets had been expecting a somewhat better figure. But nevertheless the numbers confirm that, stripping out all the volatility that is caused by construction, the upward trend is quite steady. This bodes well for the economic recovery in the time ahead. It looks like most of the strength is confined to the industrial and export sectors."
THOMAS MAYER, Senior economist, Goldman Sachs.
"The figures are a very pleasing development after the strong growth in January.
"The two monthly figures together confirm the impression that the weakness in the fourth quarter is over and that the upwards growth path in 1997 will continue."
ADRIAN SCHMIDT, International economist at Chase in London

"They were a bit weaker than the market had anticipated. But they were not that bad. In general, over two months, domestic orders are down a bit and foreign orders are leading the way, but capital goods orders in total have been fairly solid. We had a sharp rise last month so a moderate figure this month is no big deal."
